libc_deps: MicroPython set (arm-none-eabi-nm -u obj/mp_all.m4.o): memmove only. Fork (obj/mpfork_all.m4.o): memmove only. recursiveloop.c with default re1_5_fatal: + re1_5_fatal (util.c -> fprintf, exit, _impure_ptr, malloc, memset). backtrack.c: + newsub/incref/update/decref (sub.c) + memset; sub.c -> mal (util.c -> malloc, memset). No setjmp, no strlen, no memcmp anywhere.
ram_model: No malloc in the engine proper (recursiveloop set). Caller allocates the bytecode buffer: re1_5_sizecode() returns the exact byte size (12-byte ByteProg header {bytelen,len,sub} + 10 bytes search-prefix/Save0/Save1/Match + ~2 bytes per atom, jumps 2 bytes). Captures: caller-supplied array of 2*(ngroups+1) const char* (Save slots; MAXSUB=20 in the header only applies to the Sub-based back-ends). Matching is recursive backtracking: recursiveloop() recurses on every Split/RSplit and every Save it executes, 48-byte frame on Cortex-M4 (stmdb {r0-r2,r4-r11,lr}); depth = O(text length x quantifiers/groups on the path), unbounded by the library - MicroPython plugs mp_cstack_check() in via re1_5_stack_chk() to raise RuntimeError; on the host it segfaults. Time exponential on nested quantifiers (^(a+)+$ timed out). Jump offsets are int8 -> every loop/alternation body must be <=127 bytecode bytes (upstream: silent miscompile / UB - probe '(a*70|b)' on 'b' hit the fatal assertion; fork: _emit_checked returns a compile error). backtrack.c variant: fixed Thread ready[1000] (12 KB) on stack + refcounted Sub blocks from malloc.

caveats: (1) The label names pfalcon/re1.5 but what actually ships on microcontrollers is MicroPython's fork in lib/re1.5, which diverged (named classes inside [], begin_line for ^, int8 offset overflow detection, any unknown \X becomes literal X, '{' literal); upstream repo last commit 2019 - effectively frozen. (2) Numbers are -Os compile-only object sizes with -ffunction-sections, no linking/LTO; combining the 3 files into one TU as modre.c does saves only 4 B vs separate (1534). (3) Host driver has no re1_5_stack_chk hook, so empty-loop cases segfault instead of raising RuntimeError as in MicroPython; on a bare M4 they would overrun the stack. (4) Corpus counts the 7 Python-'error' cases as pass for any engine. (5) Fork's higher pass rate is partly coincidence (see difftest). (6) Not measured: MicroPython's modre.c glue (match objects, sub(), split) - that is API glue outside the engine and depends on the MicroPython runtime.
